name: Bipartite matching → max-flow
trigger: Assign / match two groups (workers ↔ tasks); "maximum matching", "perfect matching".
idea: Add a source $s$ and sink $t$. Edge $s\to a$ with capacity $1$ for every $a\in A$; keep each original edge $a\to b$ with capacity $1$; edge $b\to t$ with capacity $1$ for every $b\in B$. Run max-flow: the **value equals the size of the maximum matching**, and the saturated $A\to B$ edges *are* the matching.

name: Verify a matching is maximum
trigger: "Give a linear-time check that matching $M$ is maximum."
idea: Build the matching flow network, push $M$ as a flow, then run **one** augmenting-path search. If there is no augmenting path, $M$ is maximum (Max-Flow = Min-Cut / Berge's theorem).

name: Multiple sources / sinks → super-source / super-sink
trigger: A flow network with several sources or several sinks.
idea: Add one super-source $s^{*}$ with $\infty$-capacity edges into every real source (and symmetrically a super-sink $t^{*}$). If a per-source supply is given, use it as the capacity instead of $\infty$. Then run ordinary Ford–Fulkerson / Edmonds–Karp.

name: Vertex capacity → split the vertex
trigger: A capacity limit sits on a **vertex**, not on an edge.
idea: Replace $v$ by two nodes $v_{\text{in}}\to v_{\text{out}}$ joined by an edge of capacity $\text{cap}(v)$. Route every edge entering $v$ into $v_{\text{in}}$ and every edge leaving $v$ out of $v_{\text{out}}$.

name: Contract SCCs → condensation DAG
trigger: Reachability, mutual reachability, "roots", "drainage", counting or merging components.
idea: Run SCC and contract each component to a single node. The **condensation is always a DAG**. A **source** SCC (in-degree 0) reaches everything down its branch; a **sink** SCC (out-degree 0) is reachable from its branch — a *drainage* vertex lives in a sink SCC, a *root* in the unique source SCC. "Who reaches $u$?" → run on $G^{T}$.

name: Almost strongly connected (one edge ⇒ SC)
trigger: "Can a single added edge make the whole graph strongly connected?"
idea: Build the condensation. One edge suffices **iff** it has exactly **one** source SCC and exactly **one** sink SCC; then add an edge from the sink SCC back to the source SCC.

name: Minimum equivalent graph / transitive reduction
trigger: "Fewest edges that keep the same reachability / the same condensation."
idea: Inside each SCC of size $s\ge 2$, a single directed cycle through all $s$ nodes is enough ($s$ edges); a size-1 SCC needs $0$. Between SCCs, take the **transitive reduction** of the condensation DAG. Total $=\Sigma(\text{non-trivial SCC sizes}) + (\text{reduction edges})$.

name: Layered graph (copies) for a counter along a path
trigger: "Lightest path using at most $k$ marked vertices", a parity constraint, or "≥ k red edges".
idea: Make $k{+}1$ copies (layers) of the graph; an edge that ends at a *marked* vertex jumps from layer $i$ to layer $i{+}1$. Edges that would exceed the cap are dropped. Run Dijkstra / BFS from layer 0 and take the minimum over $t$'s copies. The graph grows by a constant factor, so the complexity is unchanged.

name: Bounded integer weights {1..k} → unit edges + BFS
trigger: All weights are integers in a constant range $1..k$ ($k$ independent of the graph size).
idea: Replace each weight-$w$ edge by a chain of $w$ unit edges (helper vertices) and run plain **BFS** — no Dijkstra needed. The edge count grows by at most a factor of $k$, so it stays $O(V+E)$.

name: Longest path in a DAG → negate + DAG-SP
trigger: "Longest path" in a DAG (NP-hard in a general graph).
idea: Multiply every weight by $-1$ (or swap $\min$ for $\max$) and run **DAG-Shortest-Path**. Linear time — the topological order is exactly what makes it work.

name: Orient an undirected graph acyclically
trigger: "Direct the edges so the result is a DAG" (or strongly connected).
idea: Run DFS and orient every edge from the earlier-discovered to the later-discovered endpoint ($d$ small → large). Every edge is a tree or back edge, so no directed cycle can form; the discovery order is a topological order. (A **strong** orientation is possible **iff** the graph is bridgeless — Robbins' theorem.)

name: Tree diameter & center via double-BFS
trigger: Any question about a tree's radius / diameter / center.
idea: BFS from any vertex to find the farthest vertex $a$; BFS from $a$ to find the farthest vertex $b$. The path $a\to b$ is a **diameter**, and its middle vertex (or middle edge) is the **center**.
